name: Trophic levels, biomass and food security

terms.definition: The position of an organism in a food chain: producers are level 1, primary consumers (herbivores) level 2, and so on.
terms.examiner: Apex predators are carnivores with no predators.

terms.definition: A diagram of the relative amount of biomass at each trophic level, drawn to scale.
terms.examiner: Only about 10% of biomass is transferred to the next level.

terms.definition: Biomass transferred to the next level ÷ biomass available at the level × 100.
terms.examiner: Losses: not all is eaten, egestion, excretion (urea), and respiration releasing energy.

terms.definition: Having enough food to feed a population.
terms.examiner: Threats: population growth, changing diets, new pests and pathogens, climate change, conflict.

terms.definition: Rearing animals indoors with restricted movement and controlled temperature to reduce energy transfer from respiration.
A protein-rich food made from the fungus Fusarium, grown in fermenters on glucose syrup.
terms.examiner: Biotechnology to feed a growing population.
